subject: Materials Science
title: Characterizing Nanomaterials
description: A quick win: understand Characterizing Nanomaterials.

hook.text: You can't see a nanoparticle with a regular microscope — light waves are too big. You need electrons instead.

buildup.text: TEM (transmission electron microscopy) fires electrons through thin samples — resolving individual atoms at 0.1 nm.

discovery.text: AFM drags a tiny tip across a surface — mapping topography with sub-nanometer resolution.

twist.text: DLS (dynamic light scattering) measures size in solution — but it reports hydrodynamic diameter, not true particle size.

climax.text: Combining TEM, XRD, XPS, and DLS gives the full picture — size, shape, crystal structure, and surface chemistry.

punchline.text: Seeing atoms needs electron beams — light waves are too big for nanoscale.

quiz.question: Why can't optical microscopes image individual nanoparticles?
options: Visible light wavelengths are larger than the particles, limiting resolution
Nanoparticles move too fast to photograph
